purpose: Scientific grounding and executable mapping for constrained activity modeling in SceneFlow generation.

metaModel.name: ConstrainedActivityModel
metaModel.description: Abstract layer for describing interaction as constraint + constrained activity + policy + completion.

fields.name: constraint
fields.description: Defines the condition that must become true to leave the waiting/monitoring scope.

fields.name: constrainedActivity
fields.description: Describes what the system should keep doing while the constraint is false.

fields.name: policy
fields.description: Controls cadence, limits, and interruption strategy for the constrained activity.

fields.name: completion
fields.description: Specifies the transition behavior once the constraint is satisfied.

patternLibrary.label: Fixed sequence
patternLibrary.humanDescription: The agent works through a series of steps in a fixed order. Each step begins only once the previous one has finished.

sceneFlowMapping.steps: one create_node per step, each carrying the command that step performs
sceneFlowMapping.ordering: EEDGE from each step to the next
sceneFlowMapping.entry: the first step is marked as a start node
sceneFlowMapping.completion: the final step has no outgoing edge and therefore ends the sequence

resourceRequirements.description: What the agent says or shows at each step. One per step.
resourceRequirements.onMissingReason: A scene with no wording is a placeholder that looks finished and says nothing, so it is reported for the author to write rather than stubbed.

resourceRequirements.description: The agent that plays each scene. Its device must resolve to a loaded plugin, or the step silently does nothing.

providedBy.via: a plugin declaring a speak or scene-playing command

resourceRequirements.onMissingReason: A plugin instance and the SceneFlow variables its config implies can be provisioned from the plugin spec, so this has a sensible default.

assistantScript.note: Usually already in the situation as first, then, finally. Ask only if absent.

assistantScript.ask: What does the agent say or do at this step?
What happens after the last step?
assistantScript.note: The generated final step has no outgoing edge, which NODE_DEAD_END reports. This slot is that warning turned into a question.

tutorialScript.instruction: Add a node to the canvas and name it after what happens first.
Open the node and add a PlayScene command naming the scene it should play.
Add a second node, then draw an unconditional edge from the first to it.
tutorialScript.verifyNote: The explainer reports a chain of three or more nodes as one sequence, so verification of the finished exercise uses the same detector that produces the preview.

patternLibrary.runtimeSemantics: The bare EEDGE chain delivers step-after-step ordering only because a step blocks. Playing a scene blocks the node until the scene has finished. A plugin action blocks only until execute() returns, so a fire-and-forget action overlaps the next step and needs a completion handshake instead. See doc/patterns/1.1-fixed-sequence.md section 2.

scientificSources.title: Workflow Patterns
authors: W. M. P. van der Aalst
scientificSources.relevance: Sequence is control-flow pattern 1, the base case from which the other control-flow patterns are composed.

patternLibrary.label: Ask and wait for an answer
patternLibrary.humanDescription: The agent asks something and then does nothing else until an answer arrives. The answer is remembered so that it can be used later.

sceneFlowMapping.ask: a node playing the question scene, which also clears the answer channel
sceneFlowMapping.wait: a node with no commands, a CEDGE on channel != "" and a TEDGE self-loop
sceneFlowMapping.store: a node copying the channel into a variable of its own
sceneFlowMapping.ordering: EEDGE from ask to wait, CEDGE from wait to store

resourceRequirements.description: The agent that asks the question.

Anything that writes the answer channel. This is the requirement that makes the capability shape worth having: a screen control and a background service satisfy it in completely different ways, and the pattern does not care which.

providedBy.via: any plugin declaring the channel under variables.writes
providedBy.note: Covers waiting for a slow service rather than a person, such as a language model composing a summary. The flow shape is identical.

resourceRequirements.onMissingReason: A screen can be created from a template, or copied from a near match and rewired. If no plugin present provides either capability the requirement is blocked, and the flow is still generated with the gap recorded against that deployment.

resourceRequirements.description: Where the answer arrives. Shared by every question in a project, which is why it has to be cleared before each one and copied out after.
Where this particular answer is kept. Without it the next question overwrites the answer, so this is a correctness requirement rather than bookkeeping.

assistantScript.ask: What should the answer be called, so it can be used later?

assistantScript.note: Resolved against the snapshot first. Offer an existing screen that already writes a channel, otherwise a copy of the closest one, otherwise a new one from a template.

assistantScript.ask: How quickly should the agent notice the answer?
assistantScript.note: Polling checks every interval and is always available. Immediate needs the channel to be an Event variable, and reacts without delay through an IEDGE.
The interval is the worst-case delay before the agent notices an answer.

assistantScript.ask: What happens once the answer is stored?

tutorialScript.instruction: Add a node that plays your question scene, and in the same node set the answer channel back to empty.
Add a second node and leave it empty. Draw a conditional edge out of it that fires when the channel is no longer empty, and a timeout edge back onto itself.
Add a third node that copies the channel into a variable of its own, so the next question cannot overwrite it.

patternLibrary.runtimeSemantics: Three details decide whether this works, all visible in doc/IntakeInterview. The channel is cleared in the node that asks, never in the node that waits, because a reset in the wait node would run on every poll and the answer would never be seen. The wait node carries no commands, because a guard is only evaluated after a node's commands have finished, so anything blocking there delays the check by its own duration. And the answer is copied out before the next question is asked, because the channel is shared. See doc/patterns/1.1-fixed-sequence.md section 2.3 for the underlying execution order.
knownLimitations: The convention that an empty channel means "no answer yet" makes an empty answer indistinguishable from silence.
With polling, the agent notices an answer up to one interval late. Immediate reaction needs the channel to be an Event variable.

scientificSources.title: Opening up closings
scientificSources.relevance: The adjacency pair, a first action making a particular second action expectable, is the conversational structure this pattern realises: the agent asks and then withholds its own next action until the answer arrives.

patternLibrary.label: Constrained Activity Base
patternLibrary.humanDescription: Minimal realizable interaction pattern: keep an internal flow alive and exit immediately when the constraint event/condition is met.

sceneFlowMapping.constraintExit: IEDGE from supernode to external continuation node

scientificSources.title: Statecharts: a visual formalism for complex systems
scientificSources.relevance: Formal basis for hierarchical/reactive state modeling used by supernode + transition composition.

scientificSources.title: Workflow Patterns
authors: W. M. P. van der Aalst
scientificSources.relevance: Pattern-oriented control-flow decomposition supports reusable construction of wait/exit structures.

patternLibrary.label: Periodic Reminder While Waiting
patternLibrary.humanDescription: While waiting for a constraint to become true, periodically run a reminder action and return to waiting.

sceneFlowMapping.constraintExit: IEDGE from supernode to external continuation node

scientificSources.title: Cognitive Offloading
scientificSources.relevance: Explains why external reminders reduce cognitive demand during delayed intentions.

scientificSources.title: Prospective memory reminders: a laboratory investigation of initiation source and age effects
scientificSources.relevance: Empirical evidence that reminders can improve prospective memory performance.

patternLibrary.label: Attention-Aware Interruptibility
patternLibrary.humanDescription: Delay or gate reminder/activity execution until interruption is likely acceptable for the user/context.

sceneFlowMapping.effect: defer reminder until acceptable interruption point

scientificSources.title: If not now, when? The effects of interruption at different moments within task execution
scientificSources.relevance: Shows interruption timing influences user outcomes; motivates attention-aware policy gates.

scientificSources.title: The cost of interrupted work: more speed and stress
scientificSources.relevance: Demonstrates interruption costs (stress/pressure), guiding conservative reminder scheduling.

patternLibrary.label: Mixed-Initiative Prompting
patternLibrary.humanDescription: Choose adaptively between automatic intervention, suggestion, or no intervention to balance automation and user control.

sceneFlowMapping.decisionPoint: select between automatic action, suggestion, or no intervention

scientificSources.title: Principles of Mixed-Initiative User Interfaces
scientificSources.relevance: Foundational principles for balancing automation and user control in timing and action decisions.

scientificSources.title: Mixed-Initiative Interaction
scientificSources.relevance: Provides taxonomy and evaluation framing for mixed-initiative decision points.

patternLibrary.label: Socially Assistive Engagement While Waiting
patternLibrary.humanDescription: Use social or multimodal engagement behaviors during waiting to support adherence and keep interaction meaningful.

sceneFlowMapping.execution: cycle or schedule activities while constraint remains unsatisfied

scientificSources.title: Socially assistive robotics [Grand challenges of robotics]
scientificSources.relevance: Frames socially assistive behavior dimensions (engagement, adaptation, empathy) for non-contact assistance.

scientificSources.title: Socially assistive robotics for post-stroke rehabilitation
scientificSources.relevance: Evidence that socially assistive, non-contact interventions can support adherence and engagement.

selectionOrder: select compatible patternLibrary entries by supportsMeta
requiredInvariants: active internal flow exists while waiting
interrupt edge has valid external target node id
constraint variable exists or is created according to output mode

selectionContract: Pattern selection matches supportsMeta against the meta a template resolved. Only array values are criteria; a scalar documents where a value comes from and is never matched. A criterion whose key the template did not resolve is ignored, a resolved value outside the declared list rejects the pattern, and a pattern must match at least one criterion. Implemented patterns win over planned ones, then higher specificity, then the order in this file. When only planned patterns match, fallbackTo decides where to land.
authoringContract: resourceRequirements are capability-shaped: state what a pattern needs, never a named artifact, so one entry both matches an existing resource and describes what to build when none exists. onMissing is create (a placeholder with a sensible default: variables, screens from a template), record (only the author can supply the substance, such as a scene wording), or block (no plugin present provides the capability, in which case the flow is still generated and the gap is recorded against that deployment). A near-match is copied with a note rather than rebound, so nothing another part of the flow depends on is quietly repurposed. See doc/sceneflow-modelling-support-concept.md sections 4a and 4b.
